can_do_statement: Can use the simple past form of 'be' + 'going to' to talk about the future from a point in the past. ► 'be going to'

ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing what was planned in the past but usually didn't happen

positives: She was going to return it but she saw something very strange.
We were clearly going to meet two days later in the square.
negatives: I am going to do it tomorrow.
She was going to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' to talk about the future from a point in the past.► 'would'

ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing future outcomes as seen from a past moment

positives: I knew it would be a lovely birthday present.
We thought that the film would be horrible.
negatives: I would like to have a coffee.
If I had money, I would buy a car.

can_do_statement: Can use the simple past form of 'be' + 'on the point of' + '-ing' to talk about things that were expected to happen soon after a point in the past.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: emphasizing an action that was very close to happening

positives: I was on the point of leaving the office.
They were on the point of catching him.
negatives: I am on the point of leaving.
He made a point of talking to everyone.

can_do_statement: Can use the simple past form of 'be' + 'about to' (often with 'just') to talk about the immediate future from a point in the past.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing that something was just going to happen

positives: I was just about to write you a letter.
Our father was about to buy a brand new car.
negatives: I am about to leave.
It was about a boy who went to space.

can_do_statement: Can use the simple past form of 'be' + 'due to' to talk about scheduled events in the future from a point in the past.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: talking about something formally planned in the past

positives: My plane was due to leave in 40 minutes.
The factory was due to be built near the lake.
negatives: The flight is due to arrive at noon.
His success was due to hard work.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form of the future perfect continuous.

ontology.mental_model: ongoing action incomplete at a future point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing that an action will not have been continuing up to a future point

positives: I will not have been working here for long.
They won't have been studying for three hours.
negatives: I will not have finished my homework by then.
He hasn't been working here long.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: ongoing action completed at a future point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: emphasising duration of an activity looking back from a future point

positives: This summer I will have been working for three years.
By then, she'll have been studying for an hour.
negatives: I will have been to London.
I will not have been working here for long.

can_do_statement: Can use the future perfect continuous to make assumptions about the present.

ontology.mental_model: assumption about an ongoing present state
ontology.pedagogical_hook: using 'will have been doing' to guess what is happening now

positives: I suppose you will have been studying very hard for this exam.
I imagine they'll have been waiting for hours.
negatives: By tomorrow, I will have been working for ten years.
I guess he will have finished it by now.

guideword: USE: LOOKING BACK FROM A POINT IN THE FUTURE
can_do_statement: Can use the future perfect continuous to look back to the past from a point in the future and to emphasise the duration of an activity or event.

ontology.mental_model: duration of an activity looking back from the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: emphasising how long something will have been going on by a certain future time

positives: This month, I will have been studying English for seven months.
I will have been working for my company for one year by the end of June.
negatives: I imagine you will have been waiting outside.
I won't have been studying.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: event completed before a future time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing that something will be finished before a point in the future

positives: I'm sure I will have learned today's lesson by the next lesson.
The role of clothes will have disappeared by the year 2050.
negatives: I will have been learning English for ten years.
I won't have finished my work by then.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: event not completed before a future time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing that something will not be finished before a point in the future

positives: I will not have finished my university exams by June.
We won't have done more than 40 km.
negatives: I will have learned the lesson by then.
They haven't done it yet.

guideword: USE: EVENTS COMPLETED IN THE FUTURE
can_do_statement: Can use the future perfect simple with 'will' to talk about something which is expected to be completed (or not completed) by a certain point in the future.

ontology.mental_model: event completed before a future time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing that something will be finished before a point in the future

positives: The match will have finished by that time.
You will have saved more money at the end of the month.
negatives: I will have finished the book.
I will not have been working here for long.

can_do_statement: Can use the future perfect with adverbs (in the normal mid-position).

ontology.pedagogical_hook: adding an adverb mid-sentence for future perfect

positives: You will surely have discovered why this man is famous.
Sales will possibly have fallen again by the end of the year.
negatives: You will have successfully discovered it.
I will have learned it by tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form of the future perfect simple.

ontology.mental_model: asking about a completed event before a future time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: asking if something will be finished by a future time

positives: Will he have changed?
Won't they have finished by tomorrow?
negatives: He will have changed.
Will he change by tomorrow?

can_do_statement: Can use the future perfect simple with 'will' to make assumptions about the present, particularly with 'you'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: using 'will have done' to guess what has happened

positives: As you will have heard, this year's programme was a success.
All of this is because her book will have included the traditions.
negatives: You will have finished by tomorrow.
I will not have done it.
